questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to get better at legal english and therefore I chose an english speaking county. I chose the school because of its high ranking and interesting classes.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was originally supposed to go to Sidney but it was cancelled because of COVID-19. I would have prefered going there. The school teaching quality could have been better and I had expected more events and stuff for the erasmus students. There really wasnt any.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a few days of introduction but it wasnt planned very well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard. It was extremely expensive and a lot was sold out by the time I had gotten my acceptance.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it is very expensive in London.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was no housing available to students, only private housing which was very expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was find although it was not described very well that there were only few possible selections of classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They answered emails quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not at all at first. Only about 7 classes were available to choose from and many of them did not seem high level or good. Luckily I was allowed to transfer a class in the begining of the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would not reccomend master students go there as the classes offered are not that high level and only very few to choose from. For bachelor students it seems okay but I would ask if there are any available classes you can swich to once you have started you semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of the classes offered did not seem at a very high level, but I was lucky to get some of the better ones. Compered to UCPH the classes was not as good quality.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: half was lectures like we have at UCPH and half was tutorial and was almost thte same ad UCPH but in smaller groups.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Contract Law
Commercial and Consumer Law
Industrial and Interlectual Property Rights
EU-Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Commercial and Consumer Law
Industrial and Interlectual Property Rights
The teachers were good especially IP, and the books were pretty easy to understand.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I applied for a visa (3000DKK) which it turned out I did not need.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was very expensive almost double of CPH. Grosseries were cheaper than DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of sport activities and clubs.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had a lot of clubs and activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sports programs and the "Get active" program was nice. You could play lots of different sports.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I took many trips around the UK with my exchange friends. I would recommend Brighton in the summer and to see Durdle Door. A day trip to Oxford and Cambridge is also nice. I also really liked Edingburgh.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, not that different from DK.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: we made a facebook group and whats-app chat with the other erasmus students and planned events and trips together through that.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing. The English people are very kind. The local food is not very good...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are very friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to swich in to different classes if you were not happy with the selection. during the first weeks this should be possible if you ask if there is anyting available. Be prepared for the expensive rent and eating out is also pretty pricy. Get involved with the other Erasmus students, make a group chat or something so you can arrange to meet up.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are very few courses available to erasmus students! (I had only 7 to choose from)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I met lots of nice people and had fun visiting the UK. The UK is much more versitile and beautiful than i originally thought.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The place I lived. It was very expensive (and small) and I had to rent it for 9 months and find my own repelacement if I wanted to get out of the lease early.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
